czech-republic/prague-castle.name: Prague Castle and Hradcany
czech-republic/prague-castle.description: The largest castle complex in the world, with St Vitus Cathedral and Golden Lane.
czech-republic/prague-castle.details: Prague Castle covers a hilltop above the Vltava, with the Gothic St Vitus Cathedral, the Old Royal Palace and Golden Lane. Go at opening for fewer crowds, and watch the changing of the guard at noon. The walk down through Mala Strana is lovely.

czech-republic/old-town-charles-bridge.name: Old Town Square and Charles Bridge
czech-republic/old-town-charles-bridge.description: The astronomical clock, Tyn Church and the statue-lined medieval bridge.
czech-republic/old-town-charles-bridge.details: The Old Town Square has the Orloj clock, which performs on the hour. Charles Bridge is best at dawn when it is nearly empty, and at sunset. The lanes around the square are full of cafes, so move away to find quieter ones.

czech-republic/jewish-quarter.name: Josefov, the Jewish Quarter
czech-republic/jewish-quarter.description: Synagogues, a medieval cemetery and Kafka sites in the old Jewish town.
czech-republic/jewish-quarter.details: Josefov has six synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery, where tombstones are stacked in layers. One ticket covers several sites. The quarter also has the Kafka monument and some of the city smartest shopping streets.

czech-republic/beer-hall.name: Czech beer hall and pub dinner
czech-republic/beer-hall.description: Pilsner, goulash and dumplings in a traditional pub.
czech-republic/beer-hall.details: Czech beer culture is among the best in the world. Traditional pubs serve unfiltered lager, svickova and fried cheese. A brewery tour in Prague or Plzen explains the Pilsner tradition. Book popular places at weekends.

czech-republic/kutna-hora.name: Kutna Hora and the Sedlec Ossuary
czech-republic/kutna-hora.description: A silver-mining town with a Gothic cathedral and a chapel decorated with human bones.
czech-republic/kutna-hora.details: Kutna Hora is a UNESCO town about an hour from Prague by train. The Sedlec Ossuary is a small chapel decorated with the bones of tens of thousands of people, and the Cathedral of St Barbara is a Gothic landmark. A half-day visit suffices.

czech-republic/cesky-krumlov.name: Cesky Krumlov castle and old town
czech-republic/cesky-krumlov.description: A fairytale medieval town in a loop of the Vltava, topped by a castle with a painted tower.
czech-republic/cesky-krumlov.details: Cesky Krumlov is a UNESCO town with cobbled streets, a castle with a Baroque theatre and gardens, and river rafting in summer. Stay overnight to see it after the day-trippers leave. The castle bear moat is an unusual sight.

czech-republic/karlovy-vary.name: Karlovy Vary spa town
czech-republic/karlovy-vary.description: A colonnaded spa town where visitors sip mineral water from a special cup.
czech-republic/karlovy-vary.details: Karlovy Vary has pastel buildings, hot springs and the Mill Colonnade. Visitors sip warm spring water through spouted cups, taste Becherovka and Oplatky wafers, and tour the glassware. The film festival takes place in early summer.

czech-republic/brno.name: Brno, Spilberk and Villa Tugendhat
czech-republic/brno.description: Moravia capital with a hilltop fortress and a modernist villa.
czech-republic/brno.details: Brno has Spilberk Castle above the city, a bone-filled ossuary under St James church and the Villa Tugendhat, a UNESCO modernist house. It is a more local city than Prague, with good wine bars. Villa Tugendhat tours need booking.

czech-republic/plzen-brewery.name: Plzen Pilsner Urquell brewery
czech-republic/plzen-brewery.description: The original Pilsner brewery with cellars and a tasting from the tank.
czech-republic/plzen-brewery.details: Pilsner Urquell invented the pale lager in 1842, and the tour includes the brewhouse and cold cellars with a fresh-from-the-barrel tasting. Plzen is 90 minutes from Prague by train and is a good day trip or stop on the way to Karlovy Vary or Cesky Krumlov.
